title: Resident Evil Zero Was a Nintendo 64 Game Before the GameCube
hook: In 2000 Capcom showed Resident Evil Zero running on a Nintendo 64 cartridge, then the cartridge ran out of room. Which cancelled console version of a game would you most want to play?
script: Did you know Resident Evil Zero was built for the Nintendo 64 before it ever reached the GameCube? Capcom had already squeezed Resident Evil 2 onto a Nintendo 64 cartridge, and it sold well enough to earn a follow up on the system. So Capcom started a brand new prequel, Resident Evil Zero, as a Nintendo 64 game. In the year two thousand Capcom showed the cartridge version at the Tokyo Game Show. That early build already had the ideas fans know today. You switched between two partners on the fly, and there were no item boxes, so you dropped items on the floor. Then the cartridge ran out of room. Capcom's programmers said the Nintendo 64's technical limits were the problem, and storage space was the big one. Capcom then confirmed the game had moved to the GameCube, whose discs held far more data. Resident Evil Zero finally shipped on GameCube in November two thousand two, a full two years after people first saw it. In two thousand sixteen an HD remaster brought the game to PlayStation, Xbox and PC. The cartridge version was never released, and it only survives in old footage and screenshots. Which cancelled console version of a game would you most want to play? Follow for more gaming history.
